title: Adaptive memory shedding, request backpressure, and fallback model pipeline
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: High variance request sizes + long-lived KV entries cause intermittent OOMs on p3/p4 pools during peak traffic. Existing soft-eviction approaches reduce tail failures but we still see 95th/99th latency spikes and bursts of OOMs when two conditions coincide: large batch assembly + KV growth from multi-turn chats.

Goal: Implement an integrated runtime strategy that gracefully prevents and recovers from GPU OOMs while preserving request latency and throughput. The strategy combines three coordinated mechanisms: 1) adaptive memory shedding (per-model and per-request), 2) backpressure throttles and graceful retries at the request-router layer, and 3) seamless fallback to compact/quantized model variants when shedding or retries are insufficient. The work must ship with observability, automated canary rules, and a default safe configuration for hosted customers.
acceptance_criteria: Cluster-level OOM rate on canary fleet <= 0.05% for 24h synthetic traffic that simulates mixed short+long chats
99th token-latency regression <= 10% compared to baseline when no fallbacks triggered
Requests marked for backpressure receive an informative HTTP 429 with retry-after and a transparent retry attempt by the client-side SDK when allowed
Fallback to compact model preserves API contract (same response schema) and is recorded as a degradations event in Console with token and cost delta
KV snapshot trimming reduces average GPU KV footprint by >= 20% under multi-turn workloads without losing prefix cache hits for hot sessions
Playbook written for on-call: detection, mitigation (auto-fallback toggle), and postmortem steps
comments: 2026-02-20 Aisha Patel: Created ticket after spike incident during 2026-02-18 load test. Linked perf dash and heap traces in attachments.

2026-02-23 Marco Diaz: Completed initial design doc. Key trade-offs: aggressive per-request shedding (drops prompts/contexts) vs. user-visible degradation. Proposed three-tier response: shed KV entries first, then reduce batch size, then fallback model.

2026-02-28 Design review (with Riley Chen): Agreed to avoid silent truncation of user prompts — any shedding that removes user data must be visible in response metadata. Design to include 'degradation_reason' field in streaming headers.

2026-03-03 Engineering sync: Implemented adaptive KV snapshotting prototype (branch: feat/kv-snapshot-trim). Observed 18% reduction in KV footprint on a 16GB model test. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4821

2026-03-05 Load test: Simulated mixed chat traffic (short+8-turn long conversations) with continuous batching enabled. Observed OOMs reduced but still present under head-of-line large request bursts. Added router-level pre-check for estimated memory and introduced per-request priority scoring.

2026-03-09 Marco Diaz: Implemented backpressure API (early 429) + SDK auto-retry hook (exponential backoff, jitter, max 2 retries). Branch: feat/backpressure-retry. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/1957

2026-03-11 Canary run: Enabled fallback pipeline to quantized-ggml model for low-tier customers. Nightly canary showed fallback reduced OOMs to 0.02% but increased average cost per token by 7%. Metrics: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/oom-prevention/canary-20260311

2026-03-12 Note: Need security review for metrics exposing degraded prompt fragments (Riley to file data-governance check). Also add e2e tests to ensure response schema unchanged when fallback triggers.
notes: Implementation split into three milestones: M1=KV snapshot trimming + metrics, M2=router backpressure + SDK retry, M3=fallback model integration + rollout policy. Plan to land M1+M2 in runtime-1.20, M3 gated by canary results and cost review.
